notebook: Sacred Ash (usable item): fully restores HP AND revives entire team on demand. Save for a gym boss fight — use it the moment a key lead faints mid-boss rather than losing the run. Worth more than any passive held item. Character select BOY/GIRL is cosmetic only.
Kanto starter: Bulbasaur (Grass) beats Gym 1 Brock (Rock) and Gym 2 Misty (Water) via STAB Magical Leaf. Best early-game pick for Kanto.

Kanto map 0 L1 catch: Rhyhorn (Ground/Rock, Bulldoze 55, DEF12, HP20 — BEST: SE vs Brock, immune to Electric/Surge) > Spearow (Flying for Bugs) > Water (covers Brock) > Meowth (skip). If Rhyhorn offered, always take it — covers two gyms from one slot.

Kanto map 0 L2 Bug Catcher killed Bulbasaur Lv7 (Grass/Poison) in two runs. SKIP this trainer unconditionally — +2 levels not worth losing your starter. Wild battle at L2 is always safer. Never fight Bug Catcher with fewer than 3 alive or under 80% HP lead.

Kanto map 0 L6 catch: Pool varies — seen Rattata/Paras/Lickitung AND Goldeen/Tentacool/Ekans. Take Lickitung (HP21 DEF11 bulkiest) if offered. Else Tentacool (Water SE Brock, SP.D13) > Goldeen (Water SE, Aqua Jet) > skip Ekans (Poison, no SE utility). Map 1 L3 catch: Cubone (Ground, Bulldoze 55 — BEST), Oddish (skip), Drowzee (Psychic — take if no Cubone).
Sharp Beak item: +40% Flying damage AND attempts Flying attacks. On Spearow with STAB Peck (50), this is effectively 70 PWR — a huge upgrade. Take it whenever offered on a Flying lead.
Kanto Gym 1 Brock (Rock): Bulbasaur Lv11+ with Magical Leaf (Grass STAB) beats it cleanly. Badge 1 achieved with Bulbasaur Lv13 after map 0.

Kanto map 1 catches: L1/L2: Kabuto/Omanyte(Rock/Water—BEST) or Pinsir. L4: Drowzee(Psychic—BEST), Chansey(HP82), Oddish(SP.A23), Onix(skip-ATK15), Abra(TRAP-0dmg). L5: Tangela(SP.A35,HP44,DEF39—BEST if TM in bag), Horsea(SP.A23/26), Staryu(SP.A23—skip if owned), Cubone. Pool varies — Drowzee NOT guaranteed at L4. TM on Tangela(SP.A35)=best Misty counter available.

Ground is IMMUNE to Electric but NOT Poison. Map 2 Rocket Grunt (Poison, 2 Pokemon) — Diglett Lv17 AND Pinsir Lv18 both fainted despite 2x SE. Map 2+ trainers carry 2 Pokemon and can 2KO your lead. ONLY take trainers with full HP lead Lv18+ AND at least 5 alive. Skip if under those thresholds.

Kanto map 1 Move Tutor (L6): options were Surf (Psyduck), Energy Ball (Ivysaur), Aerial ACE (Spearow), Rock Slide (Kabuto). Energy Ball on Ivysaur is best — direct upgrade for Misty counter. Never upgrade a fainted Pokemon.

Kanto Gym 2 Misty (Water): lead Ivysaur with Energy Ball 90 (Grass STAB, Tier 2). Ivysaur Lv17 beat her — heal to full first or risk fainting mid-fight. Always pokecenter before boss when under 60% HP.

Kanto map 2 L1 catch pool: Dugtrio/Marowak (Ground EQ100—BEST, immune Surge) > Kadabra(SP.A41) > Jynx(Ice/Psychic SP.A37) > Seaking(Water ATK30 Waterfall80—take if no Ground/Kadabra, useful for Blaine+Giovanni) > Dodrio > Mr-mime(skip) > Porygon(skip). Map 3 L2 catch pool: Kadabra(SP.A57—BEST), Mr-mime(SP.A49—skip), Porygon(skip). Always take Kadabra at map 3 L2.

Kanto map 1 L6: CHECK TOOLTIPS — pokecenter access can be behind question OR battle node depending on the run. The node that opens pokecenter at L7 is always correct choice regardless of type. Map 2 L6: Move Tutor opens pokecenter+question (2 paths); wild battle opens pokecenter only — take Move Tutor. Always read which L6 node opens pokecenter, never assume by node type.

Kanto map 2 L2 catch: Graveler (Rock/Ground ATK33 DEF39 Rock Slide 75 — BEST) > Electabuzz (skip) > Porygon (skip). Map 2 L4 catch: Charmeleon (Fire SP.A33 — BEST if Fire gap) > Kadabra (Psychic SP.A38) > Mr-mime (SP.A41 Psychic 90 — TAKE if no Charmeleon/Kadabra AND no Psychic on team; skip Wartortle if have Water, skip Ivysaur if have Grass). Pool varies by run — Charmeleon/Kadabra NOT guarantee

When team is FULL (6 Pokemon), a catch means REPLACING a member — evaluate carefully. Shiny Pokemon may appear as catches; skip if they duplicate an existing team member's type+move role. Only replace if the catch fills a genuine coverage gap or is strictly stronger.

Kanto map 2 L7: take pokecenter over item ONLY if team has fainted members or under 60% HP — it revives ALL fainted Pokemon before Surge. At full HP, take the item instead (lasting value vs zero value). Map 1 L7: same logic — pokecenter is wasted at full HP, take item.

Kanto map 3 L1 catch pool: Charmeleon (Fire, Flamethrower 90, SP.A38) — ALWAYS TAKE, replace Mankey/weakest filler. Hitmonchan (Fighting 100, ATK49) — SKIP, no SE gym utility maps 3-8. Mr-mime (Psychic/Fairy, Psychic 90, SP.A47) — skip, no Ice for Lance. Charmeleon is best Fire upgrade available; Lagging Tail pushes it to 270 PWR (note [36]).

Kanto map 3 L3 catch: Gyarados (ATK65 Wave Crash) seen in some runs but NOT guaranteed — also seen Charmeleon/Mr-mime/Kadabra pool. If Gyarados offered ALWAYS TAKE. If not: take Charmeleon (alive Fire) over dead fainted duplicate, Kadabra only if strictly better than owned. L5 catch: Kadabra (SP.A67 SPE59 — ALWAYS TAKE, release Mr-mime). Always check HP before setting lead.

Move Tutor priority: Wave Crash (Water ~120) > Fire Blast (Fire ~110) > Cross Chop (Fighting 100) > Hydro Pump (Water 110) > Aerial Ace. SKIP Solar Beam always (charging). SKIP Psycho Boost always (lowers SP.A 2 stages after each use — cripples in autobattler). Map 3 L4: Wave Crash on Gyarados ATK65 (+50% = covers Blaine+Giovanni). Map 4 L4: Wave Crash on Kingler ATK80 (best).

Map 8 (E4 approach) is LETHAL — wild battles wiped 4 Pokemon at L3, then wiped Slowbro at L5, leaving only Dragonite. SKIP every battle/? node on map 8 unconditionally. Route DIRECTLY to pokecenter at L6(o) or L7(+). Arrived at L6 trainer with only 1 alive — E4 nearly unwinnable.

Kanto map 4 L1 catch CONFIRMED: Kingler Lv29 (Water, ATK80, Waterfall 80 STAB ~240 PWR) — ALWAYS TAKE, replace Horsea. Other options: Gloom (Grass/Poison, skip — Venusaur duplicate), Ditto (Normal, skip — no SE utility). L3 trade: Porygon→Porygon2 (evolved, better stats). Replace Horsea with Kingler every run.

Kanto map 4 Koga (Gym 5) is Poison type — need Psychic or Ground leads. DO NOT spend Kadabra/Dugtrio HP on pre-boss trainers (map 4 L5 Rocket Grunt wiped both). Arrive at Koga with Kadabra+Dugtrio healthy or the boss is nearly unwinnable.

Kanto Gym 6 Sabrina is Psychic — need Dark, Ghost, or Bug moves to counter (2x SE). Ice/Normal/Ground are neutral. Map 5 trade [0] at L6 only opens trainer; item [1] at L6 opens pokecenter+trainer — always take item for pokecenter access. Arriving without SE coverage is survivable if at full HP with a strong lead.

Kanto map 5 L5 node [1] is a Legendary Pokemon catch — opens item+trade at L6 (2 paths). Always take it over the Ace Trainer at L5 node [0] which only opens trade (1 path). Legendary = live replacement + 2x flexibility.

Kanto Gym 7 Blaine is Fire type — lead Water (2x SE) or Rock (2x SE). Never lead Grass/Flying vs Blaine (weak to Fire). Map 6 L1 catch varies: Omastar seen (Rock/Water, SP.A103, Power Gem 80 — best) AND Machamp/Nidoking (no SE utility). Map 6 L5 Move Tutor: upgrade best Water attacker's Surf → Hydro Pump (110) for Blaine — highest SP.A Water attacker benefits most.

Kanto map 6 L1 catch pool VARIES by run. Seen Omastar (Rock/Water, SP.A103, Power Gem 80 — BEST, 2x SE Blaine+Giovanni) AND Machamp/Nidoking/Ninetales (no SE utility). If Omastar offered: ALWAYS TAKE, release Normal/Fighting filler. If not offered: take highest ATK physical attacker (Machamp ATK116 Cross Chop 100 > others), release lowest-utility member.

3-Pokemon trainers (maps 3+) are lethal even with full HP + TRUE SE lead. Map 3 L2: Hiker wiped 5/6 (Ivysaur lead), Fisherman wiped Ivysaur+Charmeleon (Ivysaur lead again). CONFIRMED TWICE: SKIP MAP 3 L2 TRAINER UNCONDITIONALLY every run. Map 6 L3 Hiker wiped Venusaur+Porygon-Z+Kingler. Never fight 3-Pokemon trainers on map 3+.

Kanto Gym 8 Giovanni is Ground type — Grass (2x), Water (2x), and Ice (2x) all counter it. Venusaur, Kingler, Omastar and Articuno are all SE leads. Giovanni is easiest gym if you have any of these alive. Map 7 Move Tutor at L6 — upgrade Kingler's Waterfall or Venusaur's Energy Ball.

Kanto map 7 L2 Scientist (Electric/Poison) wiped Venusaur+Porygon-Z despite Grass lead. Grass is NOT immune to Electric — it's neutral. Poison is blocked by Grass immunity but Electric still deals full damage. Map 7 trainers are lethal at 3 Pokemon Lv55+. SKIP all trainers on map 7 unless you have a true resist lead.

Item priority: Expert Belt (+100% SE hits—BEST) ≥ Lagging Tail (+100% dmg, moves last) > Choice Scarf (+50% Speed, attacks first—deterministic) > Shell Bell (heal 15% dmg, best on high-ATK physical) > Miracle Seed/Charcoal/Sharp Beak (+40% type) > Red Card (50% less SE dmg) > Scope Lens (30% crit—skip) > King's Rock (30% flinch—skip). Choice Scarf on a fast SE counter can OHKO before taking damage

Lagging Tail (+100% move damage, moves last) is the strongest offensive item for a STAB special attacker. On Bulbasaur/Ivysaur, Magical Leaf 40 → effectively 120 PWR with STAB. Worth the move-last penalty early when enemies are weak enough to OHKO.

Kanto map 0 Move Tutor (L6): Energy Ball on Bulbasaur (40→90) is best upgrade. CRITICAL: Move Tutor node opens pokecenter at L7 — take it even if Bulbasaur is fainted, to REVIVE before Brock. Trainer node [0] opens only item, no pokecenter — always take Move Tutor at L6 for dual purpose.

Kanto map 1 L3 wild battle can OHKO Bulbasaur (Lv12 fainted, Seel 5/37). Unknown type hazard — always check HP before taking wild battles. Must pokecenter at L7 (+) to revive before Misty; Tangela (SP.A21 STAB Magical Leaf) is backup Misty counter if Bulbasaur fainted.

Kanto map 1 L1 catch: Cubone>Ponyta>Machop. Non-standard: Horsea/Onix/Tangela — take Tangela (SP.A21, STAB Magical Leaf SE Misty) over Onix/Horsea. L2 catch: Diglett(Ground,ATK14,SPE22—least-bad), Farfetchd(skip), Onix(ATK13—skip). All weak; Diglett least bad (Ground immune Electric). L2 item: Leftovers>Shell Bell>Choice Band.

Pokecenter REVIVES fainted Pokemon to full HP — it's not just a heal. Ivysaur died on map 1 and came back full HP after the pre-Misty pokecenter. Always pokecenter before a gym even if only to revive dead teammates.

Charcoal (+40% Fire) on Charmeleon/Charizard Flamethrower 90 STAB = ~189 PWR. BUT Lagging Tail on Charmeleon is even better: 90 × 1.5 × 2.0 = 270 PWR. If both are offered same run, Lagging Tail on Charmeleon, Charcoal on Ponyta as second Fire attacker. Always equip type boosters on matching STAB attacker.

Kanto map 1 L1 catch: Priority Cubone (Ground, immune Surge) > Ponyta (Fire, Flame Charge 60) > Machop (Fighting 50, HP29 — acceptable fallback) > skip Gastly (Lick 40 too weak, fragile). Skip Abra (Teleport 0 dmg trap), Farfetchd, Tauros, Tangela.

Kanto map 1 L5 trainers carry 3 Pokemon and can wipe 3+ team members even with a full-HP lead — Rocket Grunt (Poison) killed Machop+Horsea+Staryu at Lv12. NEVER take L5 trainer with fewer than 5 alive AND full-HP lead. If under 80% HP OR under 5 alive, take catch/wild instead. The HP rule is a floor, not a guarantee.

Kanto map 0 L4 item: Moon Stone seen (force-evolves any Pokemon). USABLE ITEM — stays in bag until game offers "use bag item" action (NOT auto-applied at pickup, NOT offered on catch/map screen). Use on Bulbasaur before Brock when prompted.

Kanto Elite Four order: Lorelei (Ice), Bruno (Fighting), Agatha (Ghost/Poison), Lance (Dragon). Ice SE: Fire/Fighting/Rock/Steel. Ghost SE: Ghost/Dark. Dragon SE: Dragon/Ice/Fairy. Eviolite blocks evolution AND +50% DEF/SpDef — never on Pokemon you plan to evolve.
notes.plan: Map 1: L1 catch (Cubone/Kabuto/Omanyte BEST per notes [8][37]; builds 5th body). L2 catch again to reach 6 alive. L3 wild/catch, skip trainer (under 5 alive early). L4 catch (Drowzee/Chansey/Tangela per note [8]) or Move Tutor. L5 skip trainer (need 5+ alive AND full HP per note [38]); take catch/wild. L6 check which node opens pokecenter at L7 (note [13]) — take that node. L7 pokecenter to heal+revive before Misty. L8 Misty (Water): lead Bulbasaur Energy Ball 90 STAB Grass (189 eff PWR with Miracle Seed).

Kanto map 3 L3 battle: Psyduck (0/60) fainted here — wild Pokemon dealt full damage to a Water-type lead at near-zero HP. Always check HP before setting lead; a fainted lead is a wasted slot entering the boss.

Kanto map 3 L4 Move Tutor: Surf(Psyduck), Precipice Blades(Dugtrio), Aerial Ace(Fearow), Solar Beam(Ivysaur), Boomburst(Porygon), Psycho Boost(Kadabra). Kanto Gym 2 Misty (Water): lead Ivysaur with Energy Ball 90 (Grass STAB, Tier 2). Ivysaur Lv17 beat her — heal to full first or risk fainting mid-fight. Always pokecenter before boss when under 60% HP.

Kanto map 2 L1 catch: offerings VARY by run. Seen Dugtrio (Ground, Earthquake 100 — best if available, counters Surge). Also seen Weezing/Charmeleon/Machoke. If no Ground offered, take Charmeleon (Fire, Flamethrower 90) for Erika (Gym 4, Grass) coverage. Machoke and Weezing have poor gym SE value.

Kanto map 2 L3: options VARY by run. Seen Hiker vs Firebreather (trainer vs trainer) AND catch vs trade. If trainers: take Firebreather (Fire, 2 paths including catch). If catch vs trade: take catch (opens item+question) over trade (opens question+trainer — trainer costs HP).

Kanto map 2 L4 catch: Ivysaur (redundant if you already have one), Kadabra (Psychic, SP.A 48, SPE 42, Psychic 90 — best pick, new coverage + elite stats), Wartortle (Water, redundant). Always take Kadabra here.
When team is FULL (6 Pokemon), a catch node means REPLACING a member, not adding one. Evaluate catches differently when at cap — don't reflexively pick catch over battle.

Kanto map 2 L7: trainer (varies — seen Firebreather Fire AND Bug Catcher Bug) vs Pokecenter — BOTH lead only to Surge. Always take Pokecenter: trainer costs HP right before the boss with no heal after, and Bug/Fire both threaten key leads (Grass/Psychic weak to Bug; Grass weak to Fire).

Kanto map 3 L1 catch: Weepinbell (Grass, Razor Leaf 65 — redundant if have Ivysaur), Porygon (Normal, Hyper Voice 90, HP 58, tanky — best pick if replacing weak Rock Throw Kabuto), Ivysaur (duplicate). Take Porygon.

Kanto map 3 L3 battle: Psyduck (0/60) fainted here — wild Pokemon dealt full damage to a Water-type lead at near-zero HP. Always check HP before setting lead; a fainted lead is a wasted slot entering the boss.

Kanto map 3 L4 Move Tutor: Surf(Psyduck), Precipice Blades(Dugtrio), Aerial Ace(Fearow), Solar Beam(Ivysaur), Boomburst(Porygon), Psycho Boost(Kadabra). Take Aerial Ace on Fearow — BUT Fearow can faint before Erika on map 3 (L6 question wiped it). Consider Boomburst on Porygon as safer alternative if Fearow is at risk.

Kanto map 7 L4 question node wiped Kingler+Omastar (2 Pokemon dead in one ? node). Question nodes on maps 6-7 are HIGH RISK with 3 Pokemon alive — they can be wild battles at Lv55+ that deal full damage or worse. SKIP ? nodes on maps 6-7 unless you have 5+ alive. Trainers with known SE type leads are safer than unknown ? nodes at this stage.

Kanto map 4 L1 catch: Kingler Lv29 (Water, ATK80, Waterfall 80) is best pick. L3 trade: Porygon→Porygon2 (evolved, better stats). Both are strong upgrades. Replace Psyduck with Kingler at L1; trade Porygon at L3 for Porygon2.

Kanto map 4 Koga (Gym 5) is Poison type — need Psychic or Ground leads. DO NOT spend Kadabra/Dugtrio HP on pre-boss trainers (map 4 L5 Rocket Grunt wiped both). Arrive at Koga with Kadabra+Dugtrio healthy or the boss is nearly unwinnable.

Kanto Gym 6 Sabrina is Psychic — need Dark, Ghost, or Bug moves to counter (2x SE). Ice/Normal/Ground are neutral. Map 5 trade [0] at L6 only opens trainer; item [1] at L6 opens pokecenter+trainer — always take item for pokecenter access. Arriving without SE coverage is survivable if at full HP with a strong lead.

Kanto map 5 L5 node [1] is a Legendary Pokemon catch — opens item+trade at L6 (2 paths). Always take it over the Ace Trainer at L5 node [0] which only opens trade (1 path). Legendary = live replacement + 2x flexibility.

Kanto Gym 7 Blaine is Fire type — lead Water or Rock (2x SE). Omastar (Rock/Water, Power Gem, SP.A 103) is an excellent Blaine counter and survives if at full HP. Venusaur (Grass/Poison) and Fearow (Flying) are WEAK to Fire — never lead them vs Blaine. Map 6 L5 Move Tutor: upgrade Omastar's Power Gem there.

Kanto map 6 L1 catch: Omastar Lv43 (Rock/Water, SP.A 103, DEF 112, Power Gem 80 Rock STAB) beats BOTH Blaine (Fire, Rock 2x) and Giovanni (Rock, Water 2x). Always pick it over Vaporeon or Venusaur duplicate. Replace Alakazam — its Psychic niche is spent after Koga/Sabrina.

Kanto map 6 trainers carry 3 Pokemon at Lv52+. L3 Hiker wiped Venusaur+Porygon-Z+Kingler despite Grass SE lead — raw levels overwhelm type advantage. SKIP ALL trainers on map 6 unless at full HP with clear SE AND only 1 trainer Pokemon expected. Prioritize Move Tutor (L5) and pokecenter (L7) over any trainer fight.

Kanto Gym 8 Giovanni is Ground type — Grass (2x), Water (2x), and Ice (2x) all counter it. Venusaur, Kingler, Omastar and Articuno are all SE leads. Giovanni is easiest gym if you have any of these alive. Map 7 Move Tutor at L6 — upgrade Kingler's Waterfall or Venusaur's Energy Ball.

Kanto map 7 L2 Scientist (Electric/Poison) wiped Venusaur+Porygon-Z despite Grass lead. Grass is NOT immune to Electric — it's neutral. Poison is blocked by Grass immunity but Electric still deals full damage. Map 7 trainers are lethal at 3 Pokemon Lv55+. SKIP all trainers on map 7 unless you have a true resist lead.

Choice Specs (+30% SP damage) > Scope Lens (+30% crit) > King's Rock (30% flinch) when your lead is a special attacker. Flat multipliers beat probabilistic ones in autobattle. Always equip Choice Specs to your special attacker lead.

Lagging Tail (+100% move damage, moves last) is the strongest offensive item for a STAB special attacker. On Bulbasaur/Ivysaur, Magical Leaf 40 → effectively 120 PWR with STAB. Worth the move-last penalty early when enemies are weak enough to OHKO.

Kanto map 0 Move Tutor (L6): offered Body Slam (Eevee) and Energy Ball (Bulbasaur). Always take Energy Ball on Bulbasaur — 90 PWR vs Magical Leaf's 40, directly upgrades Brock and Misty fights with Expert Belt.

Kanto map 1 L2 wild battle KO'd Ivysaur Lv16 (was leading). Unknown wild fights can kill your lead. Always check HP + set a healthy lead BEFORE battle nodes, especially on maps where Ivysaur is your only Misty counter.

Kanto map 1 L4 catch: VARIES. Seen Vulpix/Oddish/Drowzee AND Ponyta/Drowzee/Diglett. Drowzee (Psychic) covers Koga; Ponyta/Vulpix (Fire) covers Erika. Diglett is redundant if you have Rhyhorn. Take Fire if Bulbasaur is your only attacker (Grass vs Erika is neutral).

Pokecenter REVIVES fainted Pokemon to full HP — it's not just a heal. Ivysaur died on map 1 and came back full HP after the pre-Misty pokecenter. Always pokecenter before a gym even if only to revive dead teammates.

Charcoal (+40% Fire, forces Fire attacks) on Charmeleon/Charizard with Flamethrower 90 STAB = ~189 effective PWR. Best Fire item in game. Take it whenever offered if you have a Fire STAB special attacker.

Kanto map 1 L1 catch: Farfetchd (Flying/Normal, Peck 50), Omanyte (Rock/Water, Ancient Power 50 Rock, DEF 21), Tauros (Normal, Tackle 40). Always take Omanyte — Rock/Water typing, elite DEF, becomes Omastar.

Kanto map 1 L5 Gentleman (Various) fainted Bulbasaur+Voltorb even with Energy Ball lead. "Various" trainers can carry hard counters. Never lead a damaged Bulbasaur vs unknown type; set Rhyhorn (full HP) as safe default lead for unknown trainers.

Kanto map 1 L1 catch: offerings VARY. Seen Omanyte/Kabuto(Rock/Water), Cubone(Ground), Farfetchd/Tauros. Priority: Cubone FIRST (Ground immune to Surge Gym3) > Rock/Water (Omanyte/Kabuto, Horsea) > skip Farfetchd/Tauros/Abra/Machop. If Bulbasaur has Energy Ball, Water is redundant; Ground immunity is the gap.

Kanto map 1 L5 trainers carry 3 Pokemon and can wipe 3+ team members even with a full-HP lead — Rocket Grunt (Poison) killed Machop+Horsea+Staryu at Lv12. NEVER take L5 trainer with fewer than 5 alive AND full-HP lead. If under 80% HP OR under 5 alive, take catch/wild instead. The HP rule is a floor, not a guarantee.

Kanto map 0 L4 item: Moon Stone seen (force-evolves any Pokemon regardless of level). Use on Bulbasaur Lv7+ to get Ivysaur early — massive stat boost before Brock while keeping held item. Always take Moon Stone if Bulbasaur hasn't evolved.

Eviolite STOPS EVOLUTION in addition to +50% DEF/Sp.DEF. Never equip it on a Pokemon you plan to evolve (e.g. Bulbasaur with Moon Stone in bag). Safe on Geodude if you don't need Graveler, but it permanently blocks level-up evolution too.

Map 0: L2 catch (Water > Flying > skip), L3 Move Tutor (Energy Ball on Bulbasaur first, note 32), L4 item (Moon Stone if offered, note 39). Skip trainers below 80% HP. Lead-type-match before every fight.

notebook: Sacred Ash (usable item): fully restores HP AND revives entire team on demand. Save for a gym boss fight — use it the moment a key lead faints mid-boss rather than losing the run. Worth more than any passive held item. Character select BOY/GIRL is cosmetic only.

Kanto map 0 L2 catch: offerings vary by run. Seen Meowth/Spearow/Voltorb AND Tentacool/Horsea/Nidoran-m. If Water is offered (Horsea/Tentacool), take it — Water covers Brock. Horsea (SP.A 10, pure Water) > Tentacool for offense. Spearow is best if available (Flying for Bugs), otherwise take Water.
Kanto map 0 layer 2 trainer seen as Hiker (Rock/Ground) this run, NOT always Fire. Bulbasaur's Magical Leaf is SE vs Rock/Ground. Trainer type may vary by run — read the tooltip each time.

Kanto map 0 L3 catch VARIES: Mankey/Rhyhorn/Lickitung seen. Take Fighting (Mankey) or Ground (Rhyhorn) if Water absent. Map 1 L3 catch: Cubone (Ground DEF24, Bulldoze 55 — best, SE vs Surge), Oddish (skip, Grass redundant), Drowzee (Psychic — take if no Cubone, covers Koga).

Kanto Gym 1 Brock (Rock): Bulbasaur Lv11+ with Magical Leaf (Grass STAB) beats it cleanly. Badge 1 achieved with Bulbasaur Lv13 after map 0.

Kanto map 1 L3 trainer (Officer, Fire): Spearow Lv15 FAINTED leading. Flying is NOT resistant to Fire — it's neutral. Fire still deals full damage. Lead Kabuto (Rock/Water, truly neutral to Fire) or Psyduck vs Fire trainers, NOT Spearow.

Kanto map 1 Move Tutor (L6): options were Surf (Psyduck), Energy Ball (Ivysaur), Aerial ACE (Spearow), Rock Slide (Kabuto). Energy Ball on Ivysaur is best — direct upgrade for Misty counter. Never upgrade a fainted Pokemon.

Kanto Gym 2 Misty (Water): lead Ivysaur with Energy Ball 90 (Grass STAB, Tier 2). Ivysaur Lv17 beat her — heal to full first or risk fainting mid-fight. Always pokecenter before boss when under 60% HP.

Kanto map 2 L1 catch pool VARIES: Dugtrio (Ground, Earthquake 100, immune to Surge — ALWAYS TAKE if offered), Kadabra (Psychic 90, SP.A38 — take if no Dugtrio), Hypno (Psychic 90, SP.A25 — weaker Kadabra, skip if Kadabra present), Porygon (Normal, skip). Priority: Dugtrio > Kadabra > Hypno > Porygon.

Kanto map 2 L5 Bug Catcher (Bug) can wipe even a full-HP Charmeleon lead — carries 3 Pokemon, sheer volume kills. NEVER take any battle/trainer node with fewer than 4 alive regardless of HP — 2 alive means one bad fight = 1 alive before boss. L6: Move Tutor opens pokecenter+question (2 paths, free upgrade); wild battle opens pokecenter only. Always take Move Tutor at L6 if offered.

Kanto map 2 L4 catch pool: Wartortle (Water, Surf 80, SP.A 28 — skip if team has Cubone), Kadabra (Psychic 90, SP.A 38 — take if no Kadabra), Mr-mime (Psychic 90, SP.A 41 — skip if Kadabra present), Charmeleon (Fire, Flamethrower 90, SP.A 33 — BEST if Fire gap on team, fills Erika/Bug coverage). Priority: Charmeleon > Kadabra > Mr-mime > Wartortle.

Kanto starter: Bulbasaur (Grass) beats Gym 1 Brock (Rock) and Gym 2 Misty (Water) via STAB Magical Leaf. Best early-game pick for Kanto.

Kanto map 0 L1 catch: Rhyhorn (Ground/Rock, Bulldoze 55, DEF12, HP20 — BEST: SE vs Brock, immune to Electric/Surge) > Spearow (Flying for Bugs) > Water (covers Brock) > Meowth (skip). If Rhyhorn offered, always take it — covers two gyms from one slot.
Kanto map 0 layer 2 trainer seen as Hiker (Rock/Ground) this run, NOT always Fire. Bulbasaur's Magical Leaf is SE vs Rock/Ground. Trainer type may vary by run — read the tooltip each time.

Kanto map 0 L6 catch: Rattata/Paras/Lickitung seen. Take Lickitung (Normal, Swift 60, HP21 DEF11 — bulkiest body). Paras has Bug Bite 50 but SPE7 and Grass redundant. Rattata is worst. Map 1 L3 catch: Cubone (Ground, Bulldoze 55 — BEST), Oddish (skip), Drowzee (Psychic — take if no Cubone).
Sharp Beak item: +40% Flying damage AND attempts Flying attacks. On Spearow with STAB Peck (50), this is effectively 70 PWR — a huge upgrade. Take it whenever offered on a Flying lead.
Kanto Gym 1 Brock (Rock): Bulbasaur Lv11+ with Magical Leaf (Grass STAB) beats it cleanly. Badge 1 achieved with Bulbasaur Lv13 after map 0.

Kanto map 1 catches: L2: Kabuto/Omanyte (Rock/Water — BEST, take either) OR Pinsir/Farfetchd/Ponyta (pool varies by run — take Pinsir if no fossil offered, skip Farfetchd/Ponyta duplicates). L4: Drowzee(Psychic—BEST), Chansey(HP82—2nd). L5: Horsea(SP.A23—BEST). L6: Pinsir, Horsea. Priority: Kabuto/Omanyte at L2; Drowzee>Chansey at L4; Horsea at L5.

Ground is IMMUNE to Electric but NOT Poison. Map 2 Rocket Grunt (Poison, 2 Pokemon) — Diglett Lv17 AND Pinsir Lv18 both fainted despite 2x SE. Map 2+ trainers carry 2 Pokemon and can 2KO your lead. ONLY take trainers with full HP lead Lv18+ AND at least 5 alive. Skip if under those thresholds.

Kanto map 1 Move Tutor (L6): options were Surf (Psyduck), Energy Ball (Ivysaur), Aerial ACE (Spearow), Rock Slide (Kabuto). Energy Ball on Ivysaur is best — direct upgrade for Misty counter. Never upgrade a fainted Pokemon.

Kanto Gym 2 Misty (Water): lead Ivysaur with Energy Ball 90 (Grass STAB, Tier 2). Ivysaur Lv17 beat her — heal to full first or risk fainting mid-fight. Always pokecenter before boss when under 60% HP.

Kanto map 2 L1 catch pool VARIES. Priority: Dugtrio/Marowak (Ground EQ100—BEST, immune Surge) > Kadabra(Psychic90 SP.A41) > Dodrio(Flying) > Mr-mime(Psychic SP.A33). L2 catch pool: Kadabra(SP.A41—BEST if no Ground) > Marowak > Porygon(skip). Always take Ground immune lead for Surge; skip Psychic if Mr-mime already owned.

Kanto map 1 L6: CHECK TOOLTIPS — pokecenter access can be behind question OR battle node depending on the run. The node that opens pokecenter at L7 is always correct choice regardless of type. Kanto map 2 L4 catch pool: Wartortle (Water, Surf 80, SP.A 28 — skip if team has Cubone), Kadabra (Psychic 90, SP.A 38 — take if no Kadabra), Mr-mime (Psychic 90, SP.A 41 — skip if Kadabra present), Charmeleon (Fire, Flamethrower 90, SP.A 33 — BEST if Fire gap on team, fills Erika/Bug coverage). Priority: Charmeleon > Kadabra > Mr-mime > Wartortle.

When team is FULL (6 Pokemon), a catch means REPLACING a member — evaluate carefully. Shiny Pokemon may appear as catches; skip if they duplicate an existing team member's type+move role. Only replace if the catch fills a genuine coverage gap or is strictly stronger.

Kanto map 2 L7: take pokecenter over item ONLY if team has fainted members or under 60% HP — it revives ALL fainted Pokemon before Surge. At full HP, take the item instead (lasting value vs zero value). Map 1 L7: same logic — pokecenter is wasted at full HP, take item.

Kanto map 2 L4 catch pool: Wartortle (Water, Surf 80, SP.A 28 — skip if team has Cubone), Kadabra (Psychic 90, SP.A 38 — take if no Kadabra), Mr-mime (Psychic 90, SP.A 41 — skip if Kadabra present), Charmeleon (Fire, Flamethrower 90, SP.A 33 — BEST if Fire gap on team, fills Erika/Bug coverage). Priority: Charmeleon > Kadabra > Mr-mime > Wartortle.

When team is FULL (6 Pokemon), a catch means REPLACING a member — evaluate carefully. Shiny Pokemon may appear as catches; skip if they duplicate an existing team member's type+move role. Only replace if the catch fills a genuine coverage gap or is strictly stronger.

Kanto map 2 L7: take pokecenter over item ONLY if team has fainted members or under 60% HP — it revives ALL fainted Pokemon before Surge. At full HP, take the item instead (lasting value vs zero value). Map 1 L7: same logic — pokecenter is wasted at full HP, take item.

Kanto map 3 L1 catch pool: Charmeleon (Fire, Flamethrower 90, SP.A38) — ALWAYS TAKE, replace Mankey/weakest filler. Hitmonchan (Fighting 100, ATK49) — SKIP, no SE gym utility maps 3-8. Mr-mime (Psychic/Fairy, Psychic 90, SP.A47) — skip, no Ice for Lance. Charmeleon is best Fire upgrade available; Lagging Tail pushes it to 270 PWR (note [36]).

Kanto map 3 L3 catch: Gyarados (ATK65 Wave Crash) seen in some runs but NOT guaranteed — also seen Charmeleon/Mr-mime/Kadabra pool. If Gyarados offered ALWAYS TAKE. If not: take Charmeleon (alive Fire) over dead fainted duplicate, Kadabra only if strictly better than owned. L5 catch: Kadabra (SP.A67 SPE59 — ALWAYS TAKE, release Mr-mime). Always check HP before setting lead.

Move Tutor priority: Wave Crash (Water ~120) > Fire Blast (Fire ~110) > Cross Chop (Fighting 100) > Hydro Pump (Water 110) > Aerial Ace. SKIP Solar Beam always (charging). SKIP Psycho Boost always (lowers SP.A 2 stages after each use — cripples in autobattler). Map 3 L4: Wave Crash on Gyarados ATK65 (+50% = covers Blaine+Giovanni). Map 4 L4: Wave Crash on Kingler ATK80 (best).

Map 8 (E4 approach) is LETHAL — wild battles wiped 4 Pokemon at L3, then wiped Slowbro at L5, leaving only Dragonite. SKIP every battle/? node on map 8 unconditionally. Route DIRECTLY to pokecenter at L6(o) or L7(+). Arrived at L6 trainer with only 1 alive — E4 nearly unwinnable.

Kanto map 4 L1 catch CONFIRMED: Kingler Lv29 (Water, ATK80, Waterfall 80 STAB ~240 PWR) — ALWAYS TAKE, replace Horsea. Other options: Gloom (Grass/Poison, skip — Venusaur duplicate), Ditto (Normal, skip — no SE utility). L3 trade: Porygon→Porygon2 (evolved, better stats). Replace Horsea with Kingler every run.

Kanto map 4 Koga (Gym 5) is Poison type — need Psychic or Ground leads. DO NOT spend Kadabra/Dugtrio HP on pre-boss trainers (map 4 L5 Rocket Grunt wiped both). Arrive at Koga with Kadabra+Dugtrio healthy or the boss is nearly unwinnable.

Kanto Gym 6 Sabrina is Psychic — need Dark, Ghost, or Bug moves to counter (2x SE). Ice/Normal/Ground are neutral. Map 5 trade [0] at L6 only opens trainer; item [1] at L6 opens pokecenter+trainer — always take item for pokecenter access. Arriving without SE coverage is survivable if at full HP with a strong lead.

Kanto map 5 L5 node [1] is a Legendary Pokemon catch — opens item+trade at L6 (2 paths). Always take it over the Ace Trainer at L5 node [0] which only opens trade (1 path). Legendary = live replacement + 2x flexibility.

Kanto Gym 7 Blaine is Fire type — lead Water (2x SE) or Rock (2x SE). Never lead Grass/Flying vs Blaine (weak to Fire). Map 6 L1 catch varies: Omastar seen (Rock/Water, SP.A103, Power Gem 80 — best) AND Machamp/Nidoking (no SE utility). Map 6 L5 Move Tutor: upgrade best Water attacker's Surf → Hydro Pump (110) for Blaine — highest SP.A Water attacker benefits most.

Kanto map 6 L1 catch pool VARIES by run. Seen Omastar (Rock/Water, SP.A103, Power Gem 80 — BEST, 2x SE Blaine+Giovanni) AND Machamp/Nidoking/Ninetales (no SE utility). CONFIRMED TWICE: SKIP MAP 3 L2 TRAINER UNCONDITIONALLY every run. Map 6 L3 Hiker wiped Venusaur+Porygon-Z+Kingler. Never fight 3-Pokemon trainers on map 3+.

Kanto Gym 8 Giovanni is Ground type — Grass (2x), Water (2x), and Ice (2x) all counter it. Venusaur, Kingler, Omastar and Articuno are all SE leads. Giovanni is easiest gym if you have any of these alive. Map 7 Move Tutor at L6 — upgrade Kingler's Waterfall or Venusaur's Energy Ball.

Kanto map 7 L2 Scientist (Electric/Poison) wiped Venusaur+Porygon-Z despite Grass lead. Grass is NOT immune to Electric — it's neutral. Poison is blocked by Grass immunity but Electric still deals full damage. Map 7 trainers are lethal at 3 Pokemon Lv55+. SKIP all trainers on map 7 unless you have a true resist lead.

Item priority: Expert Belt (+100% SE hits—BEST) ≥ Lagging Tail (+100% dmg, moves last) > Choice Scarf (+50% Speed, attacks first—deterministic) > Shell Bell (heal 15% dmg, best on high-ATK physical) > Miracle Seed/Charcoal/Sharp Beak (+40% type) > Red Card (50% less SE dmg) > Scope Lens (30% crit—skip) > King's Rock (30% flinch—skip). Choice Scarf on a fast SE counter can OHKO before taking damage

Lagging Tail (+100% move damage, moves last) is the strongest offensive item for a STAB special attacker. On Bulbasaur/Ivysaur, Magical Leaf 40 → effectively 120 PWR with STAB. Worth the move-last penalty early when enemies are weak enough to OHKO.

Kanto map 0 Move Tutor: Energy Ball on Bulbasaur (40→90) always first, Thunderbolt on Magnemite second. BUT map 0 question nodes are NOT guaranteed Move Tutors — seen catch offers instead. NEVER take L5 trainer with fewer than 5 alive AND full-HP lead. If under 80% HP OR under 5 alive, take catch/wild instead. The HP rule is a floor, not a guarantee.
